key_insight: Separating chemical interface energy from coherency strain reveals that lattice mismatch raises strain energy but does not clearly predict interfacial energy.
engineering_relevance: The database can inform alloy microstructure modeling by distinguishing interfacial bonding preferences from the elastic cost of maintaining coherency.
method: Construct coherent FCC/FCC, BCC/BCC, and HCP/HCP superlattices for high-throughput DFT calculations.
Vary superlattice thickness to separate coherency strain energy from chemical interfacial energy.
Classify interfaces by energy sign and bulk ordering tendency.
evidence_signal: Across 365 interfaces involving 41 metallic elements and lattice mismatches up to 25%, most phase-separating systems show positive interfacial energies, while most compound-ordering systems show negative values.
watch_item: Quantitative comparisons depend on reference states, structural constraints, and temperature; interface bonding preferences need not match bulk phase behavior.
paper_title: Energetics of Coherent Heterophase Interfaces: Separating Chemical and Strain Contributions
